title: Five9 Review (2026)
intro: Five9 is evaluated here as a cloud contact center (CCaaS) platform — Five9 is a cloud contact center platform known for blended inbound/outbound voice, dialer strength and concurrent-seat packaging. First-party pricing on five9.com/products/pricing (checked 2026-08-17) publishes Digital $119 and Core $159 per concurrent seat/month USD, with Plus/Pro/Enterprise contact-sales; a 50-seat minimum and usage-based AI/SMS charges apply. Scored as CCaaS — landscape award only; do not rank as a phone-system peer. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s business-communications methodology (ease of use, voice/messaging quality, routing and workflows, integrations, analytics, outbound tools, scalability, value, AI), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose Five9 when you need a cloud contact center with strong dialer/blended outbound economics and can meet the 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not for SMB business-phone seats.
verdict: Choose Five9 when you need a cloud contact center with strong dialer/blended outbound economics and can meet the 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not for SMB business-phone seats. Compare Talkdesk for published omnichannel Elite packaging, Genesys for enterprise WEM/journey depth, and RingCentral when UCaaS-first with a lighter CC path is enough. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, minimums and usage rates on the vendor site before purchase.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Agent desktop and dialer workflows are strong for CCaaS operators; 50-seat minimum and quote tiers add commercial friction versus SMB phones.
Core+ voice with blended digital channels is contact-centre grade — strong CCaaS voice/messaging envelope.
ACD, IVR, queue management and Inference Studio cover serious agent routing — near top-tier without claiming Genesys journey breadth.
Choice of CRM (Salesforce, ServiceNow, Dynamics, Zendesk, Oracle) and UC adapters (Teams, Zoom, RingCentral) is a first-party strength.
Reporting and AI insights on Core+; deeper analytics often add-on. Strong mid/high CCaaS analytics.
Dialer and blended inbound/outbound are Five9 hallmarks — top outbound score among P3 CCaaS peers.
Concurrent-seat model and 50+ seat posture fit mid-market to enterprise agent centres — strong scale, not SMB.
Published Digital/Core floors help, but 50-seat minimum and usage AI/SMS make entry expensive versus UCaaS phones. Affiliate economics excluded.
AI essentials on Core with advanced AI on Plus/Enterprise — credible CCaaS AI with higher-tier gating.

faq.question: Is Five9 a business phone system?
faq.answer: Not as a peer to SMB/mid business phone systems. Five9 is a cloud contact center (CCaaS) platform for agent queues, omnichannel routing, WFM and CX analytics. Compare it to other contact-centre platforms — not to OpenPhone, CallHippo or RingCentral UCaaS seats as if they were the same purchase.

faq.question: How is Five9 priced?
faq.answer: Digital $119 and Core $159 per concurrent seat/month USD confirmed on five9.com/products/pricing 2026-08-17; Plus/Pro/Enterprise contact sales. 50-seat minimum; usage-based AI/SMS may apply. High confidence on Digital/Core — do not invent higher-tier dollars.

faq.question: Does Five9 have a free plan or free trial?
faq.answer: No free plan is published. No free trial is documented on the pricing page. Confirm current terms with the vendor.

faq.question: Did SoftwareGlimpse personally test Five9?
faq.answer: No. This review is based on first-party product and pricing research evidence, not hands-on product usage. Affiliate relationships never influence scores.
